residencyRequirements.description: Either party must be domiciled in Nigeria (MCA s.2). A wife ordinarily resident in Nigeria for 3 years is deemed domiciled (MCA s.7(b)). Any person domiciled in Nigeria may file in the High Court of any state (MCA s.2(3)); the Enugu High Court is the usual venue when either party resides in the state.

waitingPeriod.description: Decree Nisi -> Decree Absolute automatically after 3 months (MCA s.58); where there are children under 16, subject to the court's s.57 declaration on arrangements for them. 2-year bar (MCA s.30; exceptions in s.30(2)).

twoYearBar.description: MCA s.30. Does not apply to petitions based on wilful refusal to consummate (s.15(2)(a)), adultery (s.15(2)(b)) or s.16(1)(a), or to cross-proceedings (s.30(2)).

noFault.name: 2-Year Separation with Consent
noFault.description: Lived apart 2+ continuous years immediately before the petition; respondent does not object to a decree.

noFault.name: 3-Year Separation
noFault.description: Lived apart 3+ continuous years immediately before the petition.

fault.name: Wilful Refusal
fault.description: Wilful and persistent refusal to consummate.

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: Adultery, and the petitioner finds it intolerable to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Intolerable Behaviour
fault.description: Behaviour such that the petitioner cannot reasonably be expected to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Desertion
fault.description: Desertion for a continuous period of 1+ year immediately before the petition.

fault.name: Restitution Failure
fault.description: Failed to comply with restitution decree for 1+ year.

fault.name: Presumption of Death
fault.description: Reasonable grounds to presume the respondent dead (s.15(2)(h)); absence of 7+ years with no reason to believe the respondent alive suffices (s.16(2)(a)).
